summary: Review Petition under Section 94(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 52 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023, seeking review of the order dated 19.5.2024 passed by the Commission in Petition No. 377/MP/2022. ‘Review Petitioner/PKTSL’) has filed the present Petition under section 94(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 52 of the Central Electricity Regulatory 19.5.2024 passed by this Commission in Petition No. 377/MP/2022. The Review Petitioner - _(b) Review Para 48 of the Order under Review dated 19.05.2024 with respect to the declaration of deemed COD for BKTL as 05.09.2021 and levy of transmission charges from 05.09.2021 to 03.10.2021 (along with interest) upon the Review Petitioner;_ _(c) Review Para 69 of the Order under Review dated 19.05.2024 with respect to the levy of recovery of cost incurred on account of non-levelled land for allocating bays towards the Review Petitioner;_ (n) The Commission erred in the levy of costs incurred allegedly on account of nonlevelled land for allocating bays. In this regard, the Commission has given the finding that the Review Petitioner has not made any submissions or disputed the contentions with regard to the responsibility of providing the levelled land, which is wrong. 3. The matter was heard on 28.11.2024. The Respondent and the Review Petitioner were directed to file their reply and rejoinder, respectively. The Respondent, BKTL, was a) None of the submissions of the Review Petitioner fall within the scope of the grounds of review as encapsulated under Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC, 1908, as the said averments are merely an appeal in disguise. On this basis alone, the said averments deserve to be outrightly rejected by the Commission. d) The averment of PKTSL that the BKTL’s scope of work was not complete is completely false and misleading, as the Commission had adjudicated this issue in Petition No. 377/MP/2022 and passed a detailed and well-reasoned order. Therefore, the same argument cannot be raised in the Review Petition as there is no ‘error apparent’ in the said findings. The delay caused by the Review Petitioner is clearly evident from the site pictures, where it is seen that the inter-connection facility of the Review Petitioner was not even ready up till 21.9.2021 (i.e., till the date, the pictures/ snapshots were taken). This aspect has already been analyzed by this Commission under para 46 of the impugned order. As such, neither is there any mistake/error on the face of the record nor is there any sufficient reason for this Commission to review the impugned order. (f) Regarding recovery of cost on account of non-levelled land, the Commission had categorically recorded the submissions PKTSL made in its reply to the aforesaid issue of non-levelled land provided by PKTSL. Thus, it is clear that whatever submissions were made by PKTSL in its reply under affidavit, the same were duly considered by the Commission, and only after analysing the said submissions, the Commission passed the impugned order. As such, the grounds urged by the Review Petitioner in the present Review Petition amount to new facts/ grounds, which cannot at all be entertained under a review jurisdiction. of the broader principles of Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC, 1908. The Review Petitioner is not seeking re-examination of the merits but correction of errors that are apparent from the record itself. The present Review Petition is on a limited ground, and this, by no stretch of imagination, can be construed as an Appeal in disguise as sought to be projected by BKTL in the reply. 7. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsels for the Review Petitioner and the Respondent, BKTL, argued at length and reiterated the submissions made in the pleadings. Based on the request of the learned counsels for the parties, the Commission directed the Petitioner and the Respondents to file their respective Written Submissions / Notes of Arguments, not exceeding three pages and reserved the matter for Order.. 8. We have considered the submissions made by the parties and perused the documents on record. Now, we proceed to consider whether any case for review has been made out by the Review Petitioner in terms of Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC read with Regulation 52 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 (hereinafter “Conduct of Business Regulations”). 9. Under Order 47 Rule 1 of CPC, a person aggrieved by an order of a Court can file a review on the following grounds, if no appeal against the said order has been filed: 10. The Review Petitioner has contended that it is seeking review of the impugned order to the following limited extent: 11. We have perused the order dated 19.5.2024 in Petition No. 377/MP/2022. As regards CEA’s provisional energization certificate, the Review Petitioner had raised the said contention in Petition No. 377/MP/2022, which was dealt with in the impugned order as under: Review Petitioner had raised the same contention in the impugned Petition and the _“47. In view of the above, we are of the opinion that it was the Respondent No. 1’s_ _ liability to plan and complete its system in a timely manner to allow the Petitioner to complete inter-facing work and commission its system as per the revised SCOD. In _ 16. In our view, the Review Petitioner has sought to reargue the case on merits and has prayed for re-appreciation of the same in this Review Petition. The Review Petition has a limited purpose and cannot be an appeal in disguise. 23. We also reject the contention of the Review Petitioner that it had made a submission with respect to non-levelled land in its reply dated 16.06.2023 and written submissions dated 12.02.2024 in Petition No. 377/MP/2022, as the Review Petitioner has not made any submissions disputing the contentions of BKTL regarding the handing over of non-levelled land.
title: Review Petition under Section 94(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 52 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023, seeking review of the order dated 19.5.2024 passed by the Commission in Petition No. 377/MP/2022.
